title: SpectralKrum: A Spectral-Geometric Defense Against Byzantine Attacks in Federated Learning

C-a.quote: SpectralKrum combines spectral projection (to tighten benign clustering and detect orthogonal anomalies) with Krum selection (to exploit neighbor structure in the compressed space).
C-a.locator: Section II-E Positioning SpectralKrum; both mechanisms carry a defense purpose in that sentence, and the pipeline order is fixed at Section III-A, "SpectralKrum achieves this through four stages: (1) estimate a benign subspace from historical aggregates, (2) project current updates into this subspace, (3) run Krum selection in the compressed coordinates, and (4) filter by orthogonal energy before averaging." -- so the spectral projection and the orthogonal-energy guard bracket the Krum selection, with the projection strictly UPSTREAM of Krum. The proposal is stated at Section I, "We propose SpectralKrum, a defense that integrates spectral subspace estimation with Krum’s neighbor-based selection.". Amendment 3 is not engaged: nothing here is privacy-, compression-, fairness- or communication-purposed

C-b.quote: Geometric methods (Krum, median) exploit clustering but fail under non-IID dispersion. Spectral methods detect orthogonal anomalies but succumb to subspace-aware imitation.
C-b.locator: Section II-E; the reason for pairing is that each constituent's ASSUMPTION fails in the regime the other covers, and both failures are named. The same reason is given as a tension at Section III, "SpectralKrum addresses a fundamental tension in Byzantine-robust FL: geometric defenses like Krum assume tight clustering of honest updates, while spectral defenses like DnC assume anomalies introduce orthogonal variance. Neither assumption holds reliably under non-IID data with sophisticated adversaries.", and as the design rule at Section III, "Our approach combines both signals: applying Krum in a learned spectral subspace where clustering is tighter, while filtering by orthogonal energy to catch updates that evade geometric selection."

C-c.quote: Table II reports the mean accuracy across rounds (an AUClike summary) at attacker count = 2 for each (algorithm, attack) pair. These values are computed by averaging accuracy across training rounds and then averaging across experimental repeats and seeds.
C-c.locator: Section VI-A; the composed system's own accuracy is the evidence, reported as a per-round curve and a round-averaged AUC across seven attacks against eight baselines on CIFAR-10 with Dirichlet alpha = 0.1 -- "Per-Round Accuracy: global model accuracy during training. PT AUC: T1 t=1 Acc(t), measuring stability across rounds. Best/Final Accuracy: peak and convergence accuracy. Computation Overhead: PCA, projection, Krum, and guard filtering times." (Section V-G). NO ASR NUMBER IS REPORTED: "For backdoor attacks we also discuss attack success dynamics qualitatively." (Section VI), so C-c is satisfied on the robust-accuracy branch of its frozen text and NOT on the ASR branch

C-d.quote: Our experiments test whether this combination yields benefits beyond its components, and under what conditions it does not.
C-d.locator: Section II-E states the contrast as the paper's own experimental question, and Table II runs it: "We evaluate SpectralKrum across seven adversarial settings and nine aggregation methods (eight baselines plus SpectralKrum)." (Section VI), with FullKrum, MultiKrum, DnC-PMF and DnC-Cluster -- the composition's own constituents in isolation -- reported beside SpectralKrum for every one of the seven attacks. The outcome is read off the composed system and stated as a scope condition, "Our extensive evaluation across seven attack families and eight robust baselines reveals a clear pattern: spectral defenses help when attacks introduce orthogonal variance but provide no advantage when malicious gradients lie within the benign subspace." (Section VIII) and "SpectralKrum demonstrates competitive robustness against directional and subspace-aware attacks (adaptive-steer, bufferdrift) but provides limited advantage over simpler statistical methods under label-flip and min-max perturbations where malicious updates remain spectrally indistinguishable from benign ones." (Abstract). IMPERFECTION DISCLOSED: SpectralKrum differs from FullKrum in TWO places, an added upstream projection and an added downstream orthogonal-energy guard, so the contrast is not single-variable; rule 4's benefit of the doubt is what carries the code. THE HYPERPARAMETER ROUTE IS NOT AVAILABLE HERE: Section IV-J gives ranges as GUIDANCE with no measured outcomes -- "Range: 20 to 100 for CNNs", "B = 50 balances these", "q = 0.98 works well" -- and a declared range without a reported result is not a contrast

C-e.quote: SpectralKrum performs well on average but is less dominant here because label-flip updates can remain largely inside the benign subspace, reducing the orthogonal-energy signal.
C-e.locator: Section VI-D; the claim names a constituent's signal, says what it contributes, and gives the mechanism for its failure. The positive form is at Section VII-A, "SpectralKrum performs competitively against attacks that introduce detectable spectral anomalies. Under adaptive-steer and buffer-drift, SpectralKrum matches or exceeds DnC-PMF and MultiKrum. Even subspace-aware adversaries often introduce residual orthogonal energy from imperfect subspace estimation or inherent attack constraints.", and the scope condition that separates the two regimes is at Section VII-B, "Label-flip and min-max attacks produce gradients that remain within the benign subspace. Their malicious effect comes from direction, not orthogonal deviation."

coder_note:
THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ROW THE AUDIT HAS PRODUCED FOR THE PAPER'S OWN ARGUMENT, AND IT CUTS BOTH WAYS. SpectralKrum is a composed defense whose paper (i) states in advance that its experiments will test whether the composition beats its components AND under what conditions it does not, (ii) reports the composition beside each constituent in isolation across seven attacks, and (iii) concludes with a SCOPE CONDITION rather than a superiority claim: "spectral defenses help when attacks introduce orthogonal variance but provide no advantage when malicious gradients lie within the benign subspace." That is, in substance, the procedure Prop. prop:identification_full asks for and the reporting discipline Sec. 14 asks for, arrived at independently. A4 must not imply that no one in the literature does this. What the audit measures is the RATE, and this row is a NO for the primary quantity precisely because the paper runs the contrast.

IT ALSO SUPPLIES THE FRAME'S THIRD EXTERNAL ANCHOR ON COMPOSITION, AND THE THREE NOW POINT IN THREE DIFFERENT DIRECTIONS -- which is a better citation set than three agreeing ones. Fed-DPRoC (2508.12978) PROVES a robust aggregator's guarantee survives an upstream transform. GuardFed (2511.09294) MEASURES a two-defense hybrid failing to inherit either constituent's protection. SpectralKrum MEASURES a composition whose benefit over its constituents is real in one attack regime and absent in another, and then names the property of the attack that decides which. A3 and A5 should cite all three; together they establish that the composition question is live in the literature, that it has been answered both ways, and that nobody has isolated the mechanism-level dependence the paper's screen isolates.

THE PAPER'S OWN LIMITATIONS SECTION CONTAINS THE ASSUMPTION OUR PAPER NAMES, IN ONE WORD. Proposing a spectral-plus-median hybrid, it writes: "Hybrid Spectral-Median Aggregation.: Coordinatewise statistics (Trimmed Mean, Geometric Median) outperform spectral filters on label-flip and min-max. A hybrid combining spectral projection with coordinate-wise median may inherit complementary strengths." INHERIT is exactly the composition-invariance assumption -- that a composed system acquires its constituents' strengths -- and it is written as a conjecture about a pair the paper did not test, one page after the paper measured that a different pair's benefit is regime-dependent. This is the single best quotation the audit has found for A3, because it is a careful paper, aware of the issue, using the assumption anyway.

C-d = YES, AND THE IMPERFECTION IS REAL AND RECORDED RATHER THAN GLOSSED. Relative to FullKrum, SpectralKrum adds an upstream projection AND a downstream guard, so Table II's Krum-versus-SpectralKrum comparison is a two-variable change, not the single upstream substitution FedSAC's random-clustering arm provided. Rule 4 forgives it -- the Krum selection rule is held fixed as a mechanism and its input representation is what varies -- and a reader who declines rule 4 here would code C-d = NO and make this a FIFTH PRIMARY. I record that counterfactual explicitly because it is the second row (after HRA) where rule 4 alone stands between a paper and the primary count, and A5 must report how much of the measured rate rests on that one ambiguity rule.

THE HYPERPARAMETER ROUTE IS DECLARED UNAVAILABLE HERE, WHICH SETTLES A LINE THE FRAME HAS BEEN APPROACHING SINCE DP2Guard. This paper has a section titled Hyperparameter Analysis listing r, B, trim fraction and q with recommended values and directional reasoning -- and no measured outcome for any setting. A declared range with an explanation is not an identifying contrast; a table of outcomes at several settings is. DP2Guard's beta was the previous closest case and it did report outcomes. A5's stratification by c_d_route must say that the route requires REPORTED RESULTS AT MORE THAN ONE SETTING, or the route degenerates into any paper that names a knob.

SCALE AND HONESTY NOTES, RECORDED BECAUSE THEY BEAR ON HOW MUCH WEIGHT THE ROW CAN CARRY. The evaluation is CIFAR-10 + TinyCNN only, n = 10 sampled from 100, f <= 3, and the paper says so itself in its limitations. Its own headline is a negative-leaning characterization ("Rather than claiming universal superiority"), and Table II shows SpectralKrum's Grand Total below GeometricMedian's and DnC-PMF's. So this is not a paper claiming a strong composition win; it is a paper reporting a conditional one. That makes it better evidence for the audit, not worse, since C-b/C-c/C-d/C-e are about the DESIGN and the CONTRAST, not about the result's sign.

C-d returned TWO candidates, both irrelevant (a related-work sentence about CoordMedian and a sentence about model dimension) -- the THIRTEENTH C-d shortfall, and the framing that defeated it is a sixth distinct one: the contrast is announced in a positioning paragraph and executed in a baseline table, with no ablation vocabulary anywhere (0 hits for "ablation"). C-e returned ZERO candidates. Three of the five coded quotations came from targeted reads of Sections VI-VIII.
